title: customer-attestation-and-evidence-playbook-for-on-prem-integrations
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a working guide for Security & Compliance and Solutions Engineering to respond to customer requests for security attestations, evidence packs, and technical artifacts when onboarding Redwood Private / VPC / on-prem installations. It's intentionally pragmatic: lists what we can reasonably provide, how to present it, SLAs for responses, and redaction/least-privilege guidance.

Scope:
- Applies to customer requests for security artifacts tied to private deployments (VPC, on-premized control plane or on-prem package).
- NOT a replacement for contract-level obligations (DPAs, security exhibits). Use this for operational evidence and attestation where contracts permit.

High-level goals:
1) Provide consistent, minimally sensitive evidence that satisfies common customer audit questions.
2) Avoid over-sharing secrets or operational details that increase risk.
3) Standardize packaging and reviewer flow to speed responses and minimize legal/security review cycles.

Quick summary for SEs (TL;DR):
- We can provide: SOC2 summary pages, SAS/ISO cert references, architecture diagrams (redacted for internal IP), configuration checklists, KMS/HSM attestations (confirmation of usage, not keys), patch and release windows, process descriptions (incident, change mgmt), sample logs (redacted), and signed statements of practices.
- We do NOT provide: raw customer logs for other customers, private key material, detailed internal network topology with hostnames, secrets, or full audit trails without legal approval.
- Typical turnaround: 5 business days for standard evidence pack; escalate to Security Manager for >10 business days requests.

Evidence catalog (what to include by default) — baseline pack:
1) Cover letter (one-page) signed by Security Lead describing scope of evidence provided and any exclusions.
2) Executive summary of controls (1–2 pages) mapped to common frameworks (SOC2 categories, ISO 27001) — redwood-generated.
3) Listing of applicable certifications & their public copies (links or PDF extracts).
4) High-level architecture diagram (public-facing, no internal hostnames or private IP ranges).
5) Configuration checklist for the deployed product (items checked: TLS enforced, storage encryption at rest, KMS integration, service account patterns).
6) Template runbook excerpts: incident response summary, backup/restore approach, upgrade/patch windows.
7) Sample, redacted log snippets demonstrating redaction: timestamps and relevant fields only; no PII or secrets.
8) Cryptographic statement: algorithms in use, key management approach, rotation cadence; do not include key material.
9) Process attestations: change control, vulnerability management cadence, penetration test summaries (redacted).
10) Contact & escalation list for security/investigations.

Redaction rules (strict):
- Remove or mask any hostnames, private IPs, internal WAF rules, internal ticket IDs that reveal customer names, and any token, key, or password.
- PII must be fully removed unless the requesting customer owns the PII and an approved legal path exists.
- When providing log samples, keep to <50 lines, and mask anything matching regex patterns for emails, IPs, GUIDs unless cleared.

Acceptable attestation language (examples):
- "Redwood Inference confirms that, for the customer deployment referenced, storage is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and encryption keys are managed via a customer-configurable KMS integration. Redwood does not store customer-managed keys unless contractually requested and documented."
- "Redwood follows a documented monthly patch cadence with emergency patches applied per our incident response procedures. Patch dates and CVE references will be provided in the evidence pack where applicable."

Response workflow (operational):
1) SE receives request and fills intake form (link to Confluence intake template).
2) SE adds request to team-triage Slack channel #sec-evidence and tags Security Lead.
3) Security triage (within 24 business hours): categorize as "standard pack" or "sensitive/escalation".
4) Prepare baseline pack using stock templates (below).
5) Security reviewer performs redaction and signs off.
6) Legal is looped in if the customer asks for contract-level assurances beyond standard items (e.g., source code review, full audit access).
7) Deliver via secure channel (SFTP w/ password + 1-time link, or secure customer portal) and record delivery in Jira ticket.

Turnaround SLAs and expectations:
- Standard evidence pack: 5 business days (assumes no additional legal/third-party dependencies).
- Pen test reports or vendor-supplied attestations: may require 10–15 business days to obtain redacted copies.
- If the request requires involvement of a third-party vendor (cloud provider, partner) or a contractual amendment, notify customer of expected delay within 2 business days.

Templates and artifacts (links and notes):
- Cover letter template: use SEC/attestation-cover-template (Confluence) and update product name/version.
- Arch diagram: use public_arch_diagram_v3.psd and apply redaction layer.
- Patch cadence table: include last 6 months of patch windows and CVEs addressed.

Prohibited & high-risk requests (immediate escalation):
- Customer requests for raw host-level audit trails across multiple customers.
- Requests to perform on-site code reviews without a signed NDA + scoping statement.
- Demands for private key escrow or key handing.
- Any request suggesting exfiltration of customer data belonging to a different tenant.

Examples of real-world Qs and suggested responses:
Q: "Can we get the full access log for backend X for the last 90 days?"
A: Provide a redacted sample (30–50 lines) and offer aggregated metrics and a compliance statement. For customer-specific logs for that same customer only, use a separate legal path and confirm scope.

Q: "Can Redwood perform a source-code review?"
A: We can discuss via Professional Services under a scoped statement of work and NDA. Point them to Solutions Eng and PS team.

Unresolved items / TODOs:
- Create an inventory of all currently available third-party attestations and where the canonical copies are stored (action: Marcus).
- Finalize the redaction regex library and publish in repo (action: Priya).
- Confirm whether we will include a signed statement from the CTO for high-tier customers (security review pending).

Attachments to assemble for a sample pack (checklist):
- [ ] Signed cover letter
- [ ] Exec summary PDF
- [ ] Arch diagram (redacted)
- [ ] Config checklist export (csv)
- [ ] Sample logs (redacted)
- [ ] Patch cadence table (last 6 months)
- [ ] Cert copies (PDFs or links)

Owner notes (voice-of-doc):
- Keep answers short and explicit. Avoid overpromising: when in doubt say "requires legal review".
- This is a living document — expect to update after 3 customer cycles.

Reviewer checklist for delivery:
- Is any provided item extractable to reveal other customers? -> If yes, redact further.
- Did Security sign off on redaction? -> required.
- Did Legal confirm no contract amendment is required? -> if no, include a caveat in the cover letter.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary security lead: ava.rodriguez@redwood.ai
- Backup: security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Solutions Eng contact for on-prem: se-onsite@redwood.ai

Notes & history:
- v0.1 initial draft by Ava (2025-10-15)
- v0.4 added redaction rules and turnaround SLAs (2025-12-01)
- v0.9 expanded examples and reviewer checklist (2026-02-20)

End of playbook — comments welcome.

(Working doc: meant to be pragmatic and slightly informal; if moving to a canonical Confluence entry, we'll reformat and add formal sign-off sections.)
